title: What fits what: standard parts and where to find them
summary: The standard numbers on bearings, belts, cells, bulbs, screws and fittings, how to read them, and which devices hold the common ones. A part with a standard number fits anything else that takes that number.

steps.text: Clean the part and read the number printed or stamped on it.
If the number is gone, measure: bore, outside diameter and width for a bearing; top width and length for a belt; diameter and length for a cell.
Match the standard size, then check the rating (load, voltage, current) is at least what the new job needs.

notes:
## Bearings

Most are deep-groove ball bearings numbered 6xxx: 60xx is light, 62xx medium, 63xx heavy (same bore, bigger and stronger). The last two digits give the bore: 00 is 10 mm, 01 is 12, 02 is 15, 03 is 17, and from 04 up multiply by 5 (6204 is 20 mm, 6205 is 25 mm). Small three-digit ones end in the bore: 608 is 8 mm, 626 is 6 mm.

Suffixes: Z or ZZ is a metal shield on one or both sides; RS or 2RS is a rubber seal, better against water and grit.

| Bearing | Bore × outside × width | Common in |
|---|---|---|
| 608 | 8 × 22 × 7 mm | Skateboards, scooters, inline skates, fans, 3D printers |
| 626 | 6 × 19 × 6 mm | Small motors, printers, power tools |
| 6000 | 10 × 26 × 8 mm | Small motors and pumps |
| 6201 | 12 × 32 × 10 mm | Motors, small wheels |
| 6202 | 15 × 35 × 11 mm | Motors, pumps |
| 6203 | 17 × 40 × 12 mm | Washing machine drums, motors |
| 6204 | 20 × 47 × 14 mm | Washing machine drums, pumps |
| 6205 | 25 × 52 × 15 mm | Front-load washer drums |
| 6206 | 30 × 62 × 16 mm | Large front-load washer drums |

## Belts

- **V-belts**: the size is printed on the belt. Classical A is ½ in (13 mm) across the top and B 21/32 in (17 mm); the light-duty equivalents are 4L and 5L, and 3L is ⅜ in. Classical A and B numbers are the inside length in inches (A42 is about 44 in around the outside); 4L and 5L numbers are the outside length in tenths of an inch, so 4L420 is 42 in and matches an A40.
- **Ribbed belts**: 6PK1200 is 6 ribs of the PK profile (cars), 1200 mm long. Dryers, washers and treadmills use finer PJ and PH ribs.
- **Toothed (timing) belts**: the pitch must match the pulley: GT2 (2 mm) in 3D printers, HTD 3M and 5M in machines.

## Cells and batteries

| Cell | Size | Found in |
|---|---|---|
| 18650 | 18 × 65 mm, 3.6–3.7 V lithium-ion | Laptop packs, power tool and e-bike packs, power banks, flashlights |
| 21700 | 21 × 70 mm, 3.6–3.7 V | Newer tool and e-bike packs, flashlights |
| 14500 | AA size but 3.2–3.7 V | Flashlights, some solar lights. Never use where AA cells go |
| CR2032 | 20 × 3.2 mm, 3 V lithium | Computer motherboards, key fobs, scales |
| 12 V 7 Ah sealed lead-acid | About 151 × 65 × 94 mm | UPSes, alarm panels, emergency lights, kids' ride-ons |

## Bulbs

- **E26** (North America) and **E27** (Europe) screw bases fit each other in practice. A 120 V bulb burns out on 230 V; a 230 V bulb is dim or dead on 120 V.
- **E12** (North America) and **E14** (Europe) are the small candelabra screws.
- **GU10** twist-lock bulbs run on mains; **MR16** bulbs with two thin pins (GU5.3) run on 12 V.
- Car bulbs 1156 and 1157 (BA15s, BAY15d) are 12 V and fit trailer and RV lights.

## Screws and bits

- M3 in electronics; M4 and M5 in appliances; M6 and M8 on furniture and machinery. PC cases and hard drives use 6-32 UNC and M3; camera tripods ¼-20 UNC.
- Bits you will meet: Phillips, Pozidriv (extra lines in the cross), Torx T10–T25 in appliances, security Torx (pin in the middle), tri-wing (Nintendo), pentalobe (Apple).

## Hoses and fittings

- Garden hose thread (¾ in GHT in North America) is not pipe thread (NPT): they don't seal on each other. Washing machine inlet hoses use garden hose thread.
- Fridge water lines are ¼ in tubing with compression or push-fit ends.
- Propane: 20 lb barbecue tanks have an ACME outer thread; 1 lb camping cylinders a 1 in fine thread. Use proper adapters, never improvised ones.
